name: Value private investments each quarter
summary: Every quarter the fund values about 1,600 private holdings: fund and co-investment interests from the managers' reported net asset values, and direct companies, real assets and loans from models. Deal teams propose values for direct holdings and an independent valuation group in Finance rebuilds the key inputs, engages third-party appraisers for the most subjective assets, challenges the deal teams and approves each value before the Valuation Committee signs off. Late GP statements, quarter-end financials that arrive weeks after quarter end and judgment-heavy holdings squeeze the work into the 45 days before quarterly statements are due.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager with an independent valuation group in Finance, governed by a management Valuation Committee and the Board's Audit Committee.
baseline.notes: The unit is one holding valued for one quarter-end. Monthly volume is a quarter's 1,600 holdings divided by three; in practice all of them pass through in the six weeks after quarter end.

trigger: The quarter ends and the holding's quarter-end valuation file is opened.
end_state: The Valuation Committee has approved the holding's fair value and it is released to fund accounting, with auditor questions closed where sampled.

volume.seasonality: All work falls in the six weeks after each quarter end; the March year end adds audit work.

evidence.note: Process map estimate of 1,300 to 2,000 private holdings a quarter, anchored on 318 partners, 160 PE fund managers and C$54 billion of unfunded commitments.

roles.title: Senior Managing Director and Chief Financial and Risk Officer

evidence.note: Chairs the Valuation Committee (assumption). FTE is the author's estimate from hands-on time per holding times about 533 holdings a month (1,600 a quarter).

systems.name: Private investments administration and cash flow system
General partner and fund administrator investor portals
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse

steps.name: Open the holding's quarter-end valuation file
steps.description: A valuation associate rolls the holding's file forward from last quarter, pulls cost, cash flows and the prior value from the private investments system, and assigns the holding to its review path.

next.condition: fund or co-investment interest valued at NAV

evidence.note: Mix of holdings follows fund investments valued at NAV and Level 3 split by department. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Retrieve GP statements and recent cash flows
steps.description: A funds operations analyst downloads the latest capital account statement from the GP portal, records the reported NAV and its reference date, and lists calls and distributions since that date.

error.defect_description: NAV recorded for the wrong fund or reference date.

evidence.note: Fund NAVs come from managers; annual audited reports can take 90 days. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chase the GP for a missing statement
steps.description: The analyst emails the GP's investor relations team or fund administrator for the missing statement and records a fallback: use the prior NAV rolled forward if it does not arrive in time.

evidence.note: GP reporting lags; fallback is common practice. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Roll forward the NAV for cash flows and market moves
steps.description: A valuation associate adjusts the reported NAV for calls and distributions since its date and, where the lag is long or markets moved sharply, applies an index-based adjustment.

error.defect_description: Cash flow missed or double counted in the roll-forward.

evidence.note: IPEV 4.2: adjust reported NAV for time elapsed, subsequent investments or realisations and market changes. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review NAV reliance and flag unusual values
steps.description: A senior valuation professional checks the NAV date, the GP's fair value policy and audit opinion, compares the change with peers and public markets, and sends back roll-forwards that look wrong.

control.basis: IFRS 13 fair value measurement and the valuation policy: validate reliance on manager NAVs

evidence.note: Procedures to validate reliance on NAVs provided by investment managers. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Propose quarter-end value (PE)
steps.description: The PE deal principal updates the holding's valuation model with the latest financials, budget, net debt and comparable multiples or cash flow forecasts, and submits a proposed value with a short explanation of the change.

error.defect_description: Stale financials, wrong net debt or comparables set changed without reason.

evidence.note: Deal teams supply valuation inputs; techniques include comparable multiples and DCF. Wait reflects quarter-end management accounts arriving two to three weeks after quarter end. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Propose quarter-end value (Real Assets)
steps.description: The Real Assets deal principal updates the holding's valuation model with the latest financials, budget, net debt and comparable multiples or cash flow forecasts, and submits a proposed value with a short explanation of the change.

error.defect_description: Stale financials, wrong net debt or comparables set changed without reason.

evidence.note: Deal teams supply valuation inputs; techniques include comparable multiples and DCF. Wait reflects quarter-end management accounts arriving two to three weeks after quarter end. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the independent valuation analysis
steps.description: A valuation associate rebuilds the key inputs independently: comparable company multiples, recent transactions, discount and capitalization rates, calibration to the entry price, and sets a fair value range to test the deal team's number.

control.basis: Valuation policy: fair values prepared or approved by Finance independently of the investment department

evidence.note: IFRS 13 exit-price fair value; IPEV calibration and multiples; Finance prepares or approves fair values independently of investment departments. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Decide whether a third-party appraisal is needed
steps.description: The valuation director applies the risk-based selection (size, complexity, change since last appraisal, annual rotation for real estate) and decides whether this holding gets an external appraisal this quarter.

control.basis: Valuation policy: risk-based use of third-party appraisers; GIPS 22.A.33 annual external valuation of directly owned real estate

evidence.note: Appraisals selected by materiality and complexity; directly owned real estate externally valued at least every 12 months. Share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Engage the appraiser and send the information pack
steps.description: A valuation associate issues the engagement under the master agreement, sends the model, financials and business plan, and agrees the delivery date before the committee.

evidence.note: Third-party appraisers provide independent views on the most subjective values. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the appraisal report
steps.description: The appraisal firm reviews the information, asks management and the deal team questions and delivers a draft report with a value range.

evidence.note: Appraisers are often engaged before quarter end on a rotation, so the remaining wait is shorter than a full engagement. Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the appraisal and reconcile to the internal range
steps.description: The senior valuation professional reads the appraisal, checks its inputs and method against the internal analysis and the deal team's proposal, and raises questions with the appraiser where the values differ.

evidence.note: Appraisals support the valuation process. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Hold the challenge meeting with the deal team
steps.description: A senior valuation professional at principal level meets the deal team, walks through differences between the proposed value and the independent range, agrees the value or asks for more support, and records the rationale.

evidence.note: Finance oversees valuation independently and challenges values. Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Propose the loan mark and credit status
steps.description: The credit principal reports the borrower's latest results, covenant compliance and any amendments, and proposes the mark or flags impairment risk.

evidence.note: Credit Investments holds 13% of Level 3 assets. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Value the loan from yields and credit spreads
steps.description: A valuation associate prices the loan with a discounted cash flow at a market yield from comparable loans and spread data, and compares the result with the principal's mark.

error.defect_description: Yield taken from a mismatched rating or tenor.

evidence.note: DCF and pricing models used for private debt. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Approve the holding valuation
steps.description: The valuation director reviews the file, the rationale and the movement from last quarter and signs off the value, or sends it back for rework.
inputs: agreed value or accepted fund value

control.basis: Valuation policy: director sign-off of each private holding value

evidence.note: Finance approves fair values. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Load the approved value into the books
steps.description: A valuation associate keys or uploads the approved value into the private investments system and the investment book of record for the quarter-end date.

error.defect_description: Value keyed to the wrong holding or wrong currency.

evidence.note: Re-keying between the valuation file and the systems of record; author's estimate.

steps.name: Check loaded values against the approved summary
steps.description: A second valuation professional compares the values in the private investments system and the book of record with the approved valuation summary and clears any differences before reporting.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: independent check of loaded values

evidence.note: Four-eyes check common in valuation teams; author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the Valuation Committee package
steps.description: The senior valuation professional adds the holding to the committee package: movements above threshold, key judgments, appraisal results and differences with deal teams.

evidence.note: Valuation Committee governs valuation processes and controls. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Present results to the Valuation Committee
steps.description: The head of Valuations presents quarter-end results, significant judgments and appraisal outcomes to the committee and answers questions on material holdings.

evidence.note: Valuation Committee review before quarterly statements due within 45 days. Per-holding time is a share of the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Approve the valuations at the committee
steps.description: The CFRO, as chair, weighs the committee discussion and approves the quarter-end valuations as a set, or asks for a change to a specific holding before release.

control.basis: Valuation Committee approval of quarter-end fair values; Audit Committee oversight

evidence.note: Management governs valuation through the Valuation Committee; chair is an assumption.

steps.name: Release valuations to fund accounting
steps.description: A valuation associate marks the quarter's values final in the system and notifies fund accounting so they flow into the net asset value and financial statements.

evidence.note: Quarterly statements within 45 days; annual report within 60 days. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Support the auditor's sample
steps.description: For holdings in the external auditor's sample, the senior valuation professional sends the model, appraisal and rationale, answers the auditor's valuation specialists and records agreed points.

control.basis: External audit of fair values in the financial statements

evidence.note: Fair values are subject to external review and audit. Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Late or missing GP statement
exceptions.description: The GP's statement is not in the portal; the analyst chases and the team rolls forward the prior NAV if it does not arrive.

exceptions.name: Stale NAV needs a market adjustment
exceptions.description: The NAV is old or markets moved sharply (as in March 2020), so the roll-forward is redone with an index adjustment.

exceptions.name: Third-party appraisal
exceptions.description: About a third of direct holdings each quarter get an external appraisal that must be reconciled to the internal range.

exceptions.name: Valuation disagreement with the deal team
exceptions.description: The deal team's value is outside the independent range and more analysis or support is needed before agreement.

exceptions.name: Auditor sample
exceptions.description: The external auditor selects the holding and asks for the model, appraisal and rationale.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from quarter end to approved value released
benchmarks.population: Private holdings of a large Canadian pension fund reporting under the fund's governing act

evidence.note: Quarterly statements are due within 45 days of quarter end and the annual report within 60 days, so valuations must be approved roughly a week or two earlier. The p50 and p90 are the author's reading.

benchmarks.unit: CAD millions change in net assets from reasonable alternative assumptions, March 31, 2022

benchmarks.population: Private market investments under GIPS for asset owners
Directly owned real estate under GIPS for asset owners
ILPA recommended practice for private funds

pain_points.description: GP statements arrive late, so fund values are rolled forward from older NAVs and trued up a quarter later.

evidence.note: IPEV adjustments for NAV time lag; 90-day annual reporting.

pain_points.description: Portfolio company quarter-end numbers arrive two to three weeks after quarter end, leaving little time for independent analysis, appraisals and challenge before the 45-day deadline.

evidence.note: 45-day statutory deadline; arrival time is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Values are re-keyed from spreadsheets into the private investments system and the book of record and then checked by hand.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Judgment-heavy holdings produce disagreements between deal teams, appraisers and the valuation group that take meetings to settle.

evidence.note: Level 3 values could move by minus C$8.6 billion to plus C$10.1 billion under reasonable alternative assumptions.

assumptions: Holding mix per quarter: 55% fund and co-investment interests at NAV, 30% direct equity and real assets (45% PE, 55% RA), 15% private loans; estimated from the org file's holding counts and the Level 3 split.

About 35% of direct holdings get a third-party appraisal in a given quarter, consistent with appraisals for most direct investments on a rotation and annual external valuation of directly owned real estate.
The Valuation Committee is assumed to be chaired by the CFRO with the controller, head of Valuations and head of Risk; its membership is not published.
Committee and approval steps carry only the per-holding share of meeting time; most holdings are approved in bulk and only material ones are discussed.

Waits are set so that holdings reach the committee about four to five weeks after quarter end; the simulator treats holdings independently, while in practice the committee date is the same for all of them.
Hands-on time for direct holdings (about 15 hours each) dominates the staffing; fund holdings take about 1.5 hours each.
The volume is quarterly work spread over three months as the organisation file does; peak load in the six weeks after quarter end is about twice the average.
